question.text: Under the distributor-manager economics, the phrase 'skin-in-the-game' refers to which of the following obligations of the sponsor / manager?

answer.text: A goodwill deposit with SEBI at the time of registration
A continuing financial interest in the AIF to align interests with LPs (2.5%/INR 5 cr for Cat I/II, 5%/INR 10 cr for Cat III — whichever is lower)
A mandatory INR 1 crore insurance cover on the Manager's key employees
A personal guarantee by the Manager for all LP commitments

explanation.text: The Logic: Footnote 70 of Chapter 8: skin-in-the-game = manager bears financial risk by investing alongside LPs, ensuring alignment on common risk-return objective. Quantum is the sponsor-commitment rule (2.5%/INR 5 cr or 5%/INR 10 cr). The Trap: Option A fabricates a deposit. Option C is a valid but unrelated risk concept. Option D is a personal guarantee — absent from AIF regs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C all test skin-in-the-game; XIX-C emphasises it as a structuring design decision.
